engagement_title: Aldervale Mutual autumn renewal drop: build a live personalised mailer out of the only artwork left, a printer's PDF, put each household's own producer on their own card, and recover the mark off a business card in a wallet
vertical: Finance and insurance, a sixty two year old regional mutual carrier writing home and farm cover through eleven local producers across rural Vermont
real_brief_anchor: Anchored to the Freelancer.com brand-collateral post quoted in the ledger's grounding_note: a regional broker asking for a fixed brand-locked template populated from a structured roster into a press-ready PDF plus an editable source, insisting that 'the colors, fonts and overall layout from the brand style guide' come through clearly and that 'I don't want to hunt for missing fonts or mismatched data'. The real post names no client, so the line is laundered to the coined fictional carrier Aldervale Mutual Assurance; no real company, carrier, agency, person, product or trademark appears anywhere, and the earlier working name that collided with a live Rhode Island carrier is fully removed. The prior version of this engagement sat on the data merge alone, which is what the REBUILD verdict is about. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: a bare printer's PDF can now be reverse engineered into a live merge template headlessly, a per row image column genuinely binds a different photograph to every record, and an ink level trace off a photographed printed card recovers a real mark. So this is that broker's actual job, end to end: the template is recovered rather than assumed, the producers' faces are real faces, and the editable source they asked for exists.
client_one_liner: Our renewal postcard has to go out in October with every household's own name, their own producer's face and their own offer on it, and all we still have is the printer's PDF, a spreadsheet and a photo of a business card.
client_brief:
Aldervale Mutual Assurance, autumn renewal mailing

We are a regional mutual in Vermont, sixty two years old, writing home and farm cover through eleven local producers. Renewal season opens in October, and the piece that actually moves our book is a postcard that lands in the mailbox carrying the household's own name and the name and face of the producer who covers their town.

What we have. Our printer still holds the artwork from last spring's card as a PDF, and that is now the only form of it that exists, because our designer retired and took her drive with her. We have this drop's household list, cleaned: about sixty homes, each row carrying the household, the mailing address, the producer assigned to that town and the renewal offer band the household qualifies for. Our eleven producers were photographed at the regional meeting and afterwards by whoever happened to have a camera.

What we need. The full run as one file the mail house can print, one household per card, every card carrying that household's own address, its own producer with that producer's photograph, and its own offer line. We also need each producer's own cards pulled out and named for them, because they hand deliver in their own towns and none of them will sort sixty cards.

Our mark is a problem. The only clean version left is printed on a business card one of the producers still had in his wallet. We need it back as artwork we can put anywhere at any size, including reversed out of our green.

Last, a small digital set we can edit ourselves next season, since the offer dates move every year: the card front, an email header and a square one for the town pages, all in one working file.

We are not a discount carrier. Our households are forty to seventy and many have been with us for decades. They should feel written to, not marketed at. Tell us anything you find that we ought to know before this goes to the printer.
price_band_and_audience: A mutual whose average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year, sold face to face by a producer the household knows by name, to owners aged forty to seventy in towns under four thousand people. The band is load-bearing. At this register the card is restrained: one photograph, a serif voice, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer's name larger than the offer. Push it down into the mass renewal blast register (bright panel, a percentage in the largest type on the card, three benefit bullets, a starburst) and a household insured here for thirty years reads it as churn marketing from a carrier that has stopped knowing them, which is exactly the retention the drop exists to protect. Push it up into private wealth register (cream stock feel, all small caps, no photograph, almost no offer) and it stops being a renewal reminder for a farmhouse policy. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even when every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Cover from people who know your town
brand_identity.sector: A regional mutual carrier writing home and farm cover, sold face to face through local producers across rural Vermont.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 1963, chartered in central Vermont, a small mutual placing business through eleven local producers in towns under four thousand people.
brand_identity.about: Aldervale is a policyholder owned mutual that has insured Vermont homes and working farms for sixty two years. Cover is written and renewed in person by a producer the household knows by name, not through a call centre or a comparison site. The promise is continuity: the same carrier, the same face, decade after decade.
brand_identity.audience: Homeowners and farm owners aged forty to seventy in small Vermont towns, many insured here for decades, who value a known producer and a fair renewal over the lowest online quote.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Average home policy runs 1,100 to 1,900 dollars a year. Mid market and relationship led, not a discount carrier and not a private wealth boutique. Communications stay restrained: one photograph, generous margins, the offer stated once and quietly, the producer named larger than the offer.
brand_identity.typography: A quiet serif system as set in the 2019 style guide: a text serif for policy copy and addresses, paired with a slightly heavier serif for producer names and headings. Editorial rather than promotional, generous leading, no condensed or display faces.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct and adult. We write to the household, never at the market, and we never oversell. Example line the brand would write: "Your renewal is due in October, and your producer, will be glad to walk it through with you."
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The original design files are gone: the designer retired and took her drive, so the last renewal card survives only as the printer's press PDF. The mark exists cleanly only where it was printed on a producer's business card. One 2019 style guide page (house green, warm grey, the two type families, clear space, and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph) is all the written guidance that remains.
brand_identity.values: Continuity and knowing the policyholder. Households should feel written to by a carrier that still knows them, and the mark is never placed over a photograph.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_renewal_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The press PDF of last spring's renewal postcard, held by the printer, single page, both sides, real embedded font subsets.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This is the card exactly as it printed last spring. It is the only form of the artwork that still exists."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed card visually separates into a salutation, an address block, a producer line and an offer band converts into far fewer frames than that, because the whole left column was set as one continuous flow, so the fields cannot be addressed as separate frames and must be reached by position inside a single story. Worse, the mapping readout of that story omits one run entirely while keeping its line break, so the string still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length, the validator returns VALID with no warnings, the placeholder step reports success, and the mappings past the omission are silently absent from the template.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_producers/ (11 portraits, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: Producer headshots, some taken at the regional meeting against the hotel's cream function room wall, some taken later outside an office by a colleague on a full frame body.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our eleven producers. Taken at the regional meeting and afterwards by whoever had a camera, so they are a mixed bag."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The frames are far larger than the one call knockout expects, and that tool silently reduces oversized inputs while reporting it in no message and no error, only as a downscaled entry inside the returned tradeoffs object. Separately, the four shot against the cream function room wall sit at almost the value of that wall at the shoulder and collar, so subject detection has no contrast there and returns a cut edge that looks clean against white and bites visibly once the cutout lands on the card's own green band. Three files are named for the branch office rather than the person, so which face belongs to which producer cannot be settled from the filenames.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_households.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The cleaned drop list: about sixty rows carrying household name, address lines, town, state, ZIP, assigned producer and renewal offer band.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's list, cleaned. Sixty homes in this drop."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: A dozen or so households carry a materially longer address than the rest: a second line, an apartment or unit designator, a long town name, a rural route. The card's address frame is fixed and does not spill or reflow, so those records do not push the layout, they simply stop rendering partway and lose their last line at trim while the merge reports complete success. Two offer band strings are also much longer than the rest for the same reason. Nothing in the sheet marks these rows.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_producer_card.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: Handheld photograph of a printed agency business card lying on a desk, the mark on it in two inks on uncoated stock: an oak leaf inside a shield ring, set beside small caps type and separated by a hairline rule.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The only clean version of our mark left. One of the producers still had this card in his wallet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: It is a compound lockup photographed on a substrate, which behaves nothing like a flat scan. A prompt naming the card returns the card. A prompt naming the whole lockup returns the type and silently drops the shield ring and the hairline rule while looking entirely plausible. Background removal on the shield returns a solid opaque disc because an enclosed interior cannot be punched, and the trace that does work arrives with no viewBox and an opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath it. The two inks also run close in value along the shadowed right edge of the card.

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_brand_sheet.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: One page from the 2019 style guide: the house green and the secondary warm grey, the two type families by name, the mark's minimum clear space and the rule that the mark never sits on a photograph.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our style guide page. Please keep to it."

assets_supplied.name: aldervale_offer_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the four offer band sentences as approved by the carrier's compliance reviewer, the renewal deadline, and the standing regulatory line that must appear on every card.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The offer wording as compliance approved it. None of this can be reworded."

acceptance_bar: One press file for the mail house in which the page count is exactly the row count of the drop list and the pages follow the order the file was merged in, with no page carrying a second household's data.
Every card's address block is complete at trim, last line and postal code included. A record whose address cannot be set completely is named to us in writing, not shipped with its ending missing.
Every field the card carries actually lands in the template. A template that reports success while holding fewer fields than the card shows is a failed template, however clean the report reads.
Each card carries the photograph of the producer assigned to that household. One face repeated across the run, or a face on the wrong town, is a total failure of the drop.
The producer cutouts hold their edge where they meet the house green on the card, not only against white at preview scale, and the eleven read as one set rather than eleven separate photographs.

Eleven per producer files, each named for its producer and containing that producer's households and no one else's, with identity guaranteed rather than inferred from the position an output came back in.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable, no opaque rectangle riding underneath it, its shield ring and hairline rule intact at the size it actually reproduces on the card, and legible reversed out of the house green.
No delivered file exceeds the pixel dimensions of the frame it came from, and no crop or knockout report in the run carries an upscale entry.

The digital set is one working file we can edit next season, holding the card front, the email header and the square, each at its own size, with live text and the mark as real shapes rather than a picture of a layout.
What can and cannot be promised to the printer about trim and bleed is stated plainly in writing rather than assumed, along with the type actually used by role.
The written note tells us the things we could not have known: what the list does to the layout, what the photographs do to the cards, and anything about the mark we should be careful with.

adobe_surfaces.surface: InDesign document conversion, template archaeology, data merge and render
adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (as mapping author and as validator), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange All and per producer ranges, additionalImageFiles bound to an @ prefixed column), document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The whole variable data spine. The printer's flat PDF is converted into a live document, its true frame inventory and true story text are read out of the round tripped IDML rather than believed from the readout, a mapping is authored against that truth, placeholders are written and then re-verified by exporting again, and the drop is merged one household per page. The same merged document yields the single press file in mail house order and the eleven per producer subsets by range.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, counting image_vectorize here rather than as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_inline_preview, image_auto_straighten, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_select_by_prompt with returnBbox, image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading tradeoffs, detection_confidence, upscale_factor), image_remove_background (transparent and backgroundColor), image_fill_area, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every raster decision. It brings eleven portraits shot in two rooms to one look, knocks them out onto the card's own ground by whichever route each frame's shoulder contrast allows, crops each to the template's real portrait proportion without enlarging, and recovers the mark at ink level off a photographed business card, including the vector hygiene the trace does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The digital set the carrier edits itself next season, as one native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, including the card front at true postcard trim in absolute units. Every photograph must be carried as image data because a reference renders as an empty grey box at full success, and the recovered mark goes in as inline vector so it stays vector.

Reconciles the two family names printed on a 2019 style sheet against what is licensable today, establishes the real numeric weights, which cannot be inferred from a style name, and produces the kit the digital set is typeset from. Where a named family is gone the substitution is the agent's own art direction and has to hold the mutual's register.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Stock and Adobe Boards, counted as ONE surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_search (entityScope StockAsset, short queries, contentType filter, never orientation), asset_license_and_download_stock, boards_create_new_board, boards_add_items_to_board
adobe_surfaces.role: Sources the one frame the carrier does not own, a quiet New England autumn property exterior for the email header and the square, IP clean, at camera scale and free of generative candidates. The Boards half persists the sign off set the branch managers approve from, placed within the per call cap with a partial result read as partial.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier and the authoring playbook, settle which deliverable lands on which surface, then upload every supplied asset and hold each returned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: The run is variable data work against a real document; the digital set needs an authored fixed canvas document because the carrier edits it next season. The merge binds images by filename, so the manifest is what keeps a face attached to a producer forty artefacts later.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming a surface per deliverable, the confirmed tier that gates the export, and a manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's card PDF into a live document, then export the IDML and read what the conversion actually produced: frame counts, bounds and proportions, applied faces and sizes.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows a designer's blocks; what the conversion exposes is a different thing and is not under anyone's control. The mapping strategy, the portrait crop ratio and whether an image can be bound at all depend on this inventory rather than on the card's appearance.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory with per frame bounds and the portrait frame's real proportion.

trajectory.action: Ask for the mapping readout against the drop list, then reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML's own content runs and compute every offset from that reconstruction.
trajectory.judgement: The readout is a convenience, not a source of truth. The only channel carrying the document's actual text is the IDML, and offsets computed anywhere else are guesses that will validate cleanly.
trajectory.produces: A mapping authored against reconstructed story text, with each field's action and position.

trajectory.action: Preview all eleven portraits and triage them: room, tilt, shoulder contrast against the ground, and which of the three ambiguously named files shows which producer.
trajectory.judgement: The carrier asserts eleven producers and eleven files, but only the faces can settle which file is whose, since the drop list assigns towns to names rather than to filenames. Getting it wrong puts a stranger's face on sixty households' mail.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note and a file to producer reconciliation.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level, then fix one portrait target from the best lit frame and bring each of the eleven toward it with its own call, recording the parameters applied.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a set of eleven faces appearing in the same place on cards going to the same towns, not eleven good headshots, so one batched parameter set is exactly wrong for two rooms.
trajectory.produces: Eleven corrected masters at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Knock the eleven out onto the card's own ground, reading every returned tradeoffs object rather than the success line, and inspect each cut edge on that ground rather than against white.
trajectory.judgement: Two routes exist and the frames do not all deserve the same one. The tradeoffs array is the only channel reporting what the tool did to a frame's dimensions and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Eleven producer plates on the card ground with their returned tradeoffs recorded.

trajectory.action: Crop each plate to the portrait frame's real proportion established at conversion, face optically placed rather than centred, and name each file to the value the drop list's image column carries.
trajectory.judgement: Optical placement on a headshot is not centring, and the merge binds by exact filename, so the naming convention is functional rather than housekeeping.
trajectory.produces: Eleven named producer images at or below source scale, ready to bind.

trajectory.action: Write the placeholders into the converted document with the mapping passed as a single stringified object, then export the IDML again and confirm by inspection that every expected field is present.
trajectory.judgement: Preparation reports success whether or not the mappings landed. The only evidence the template holds all of its fields is the round tripped document, and looking is cheap next to a sixty card reprint.
trajectory.produces: A live merge template with a written field by field confirmation.

trajectory.action: Merge the drop list against the template with the producer images supplied as additional image files bound to the list's image column, taking the result as one press file in mail house order.
trajectory.judgement: The image column is the difference between a personalised run and sixty copies of one card, and the order the file merges in is the order the mail house prints in.
trajectory.produces: One multi page press file, one household per page, each carrying its own producer.

trajectory.action: Render the merged run and read the pages: every address block to its final line, every offer line, every face against the town it went to, not page one only.
trajectory.judgement: A merge that completes tells you the mechanism ran, not that sixty cards are mailable, and the households whose data is longest are the ones that will not announce themselves.
trajectory.produces: A page by page read of the run with every defective record named.

trajectory.action: Produce the eleven per producer subsets by range against a list grouped by producer, naming each file for its producer on download.
trajectory.judgement: The master's order and a producer's contiguous block cannot both live in one file, and identity has to be guaranteed by how the subset was requested rather than inferred from the position an output came back in.
trajectory.produces: Eleven named per producer files, each holding only that producer's households.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the business card: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop driven by the selection's returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions no tool makes: how to word the selection so it takes ink rather than stock, which polarity to trace, and whether the two colour mark or a colour accurate plate is the deliverable. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed shield.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant.

trajectory.action: Check the families the 2019 style sheet names against what is licensable now, pull the style inventories for real numeric weights and build one kit; then license one camera scale property exterior on short generic queries, photography only, generative candidates excluded, and bring it to the portrait set's world.
trajectory.judgement: A style sheet records a decision made seven years ago, not a licence, so a substitution is the agent's own art direction judged against a mutual writing farm cover. A stock frame that stays a stock photograph beside eleven real faces reads as bought.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and weight per role, plus one licensed IP clean frame graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained document with three roots at three canvas sizes, the card front in absolute print units, every photograph carried as image data, the mark placed as inline vector inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, and family and weight declared on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a reference is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how quietly the offer sits.
trajectory.produces: One export ready source document carrying the whole digital set, retained as a durable deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check and export, verifying through both available channels (the document's rendition for the first canvas, the returned per canvas markup for the other two), then create the branch managers' sign off board within the per call placement cap and write the note.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning and the rendition only ever shows the first artboard, so looking at the card front is not looking at the deliverable. A partial board result is partial, and vector artwork belongs in the note rather than on the board.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document verified across all three canvases, a persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the template the client's own PDF produces can actually hold all of the card's fields. The mapping readout for this document omits one text run entirely while keeping its line break, so the story string it hands back still reads as well formed and every offset past the omission is short by exactly that run's length. The validator returns VALID with zero warnings on those offsets, the placeholder step returns completed successfully, and the fields past the omission are simply absent from the prepared template. Which run is omitted, and therefore which fields fall off the end, is a property of this converted document and appears in no response, warning or error. It is visible only by round tripping the prepared document and reading its story against the card.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it, because the omission is inside the only readout the tools offer and every mapping strategy consumes that readout. Doing it right first time presumes already knowing that this document's readout drops a run, which is document specific. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks for a card carrying each household's own details and says nothing about how the artwork converts, and the acceptance line about every field landing is the client's requirement rather than a disclosure. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different derivation of the mapping, computed from reconstructed content runs rather than from the readout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Reconstruct the true story text from the round tripped document's own content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping, prepare again and verify field by field by inspection rather than by response, before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Sixty renewal cards printed and mailed with the producer line and the offer line missing, after a run in which the validator, the preparation step and the merge all reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What this list does to this card. The address frame is fixed and does not spill or reflow, so a household whose address runs longer than last year's typical row does not push the layout or throw an error: the frame stops rendering partway and the record loses its final line at trim, postal code included, while the merge reports every record complete. Which households this happens to depends on the frame's real bounds and set size against each row's actual string, and no readout reports it. It exists only on the rendered pages, and only on some of them.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter prevents it, because the frame cannot be resized through this surface at all; the fit is only discoverable once real rows are set in the real frame. (b) Nothing states it: the list is described as cleaned, and the acceptance line about complete address blocks is the standing requirement of any mail run rather than a warning that some will truncate. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a per record copy fit decision, which is different work from merging again.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Read every page rather than the first, name the households that will not set, decide per record whether the address can be legitimately fitted (a combined line, a standard state abbreviation, a dropped unit prefix) or whether the record has to be flagged back to the carrier, apply those decisions to the data, merge again and re-read the affected pages.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A dozen or more cards going to the mail house with the postal line missing, which the mail house will either return or post undeliverable, in the one drop of the year that exists to keep long standing households from leaving.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one call knockout gives back a portrait the card can use. Two things are reported nowhere except inside the returned tradeoffs object: the tool silently reduces these oversized frames and does not restore the size afterwards, so a plate can come back below what the card's portrait frame needs, and the only route back is interpolation, which the crop tool performs to a hard cap while again saying so only in its own tradeoffs. Separately, the frames shot against the cream function room wall carry almost no value difference at the shoulder and collar, so a cut edge that looks clean against white bites visibly once the plate sits on the card's green band. Which of the eleven behave this way is a property of each frame's own contrast, and neither fact appears in any success message.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering does not dodge it: the defensible sequence is straighten, correct, knock out at source scale and only then crop, precisely so the edge is judged after it exists, and there is no parameter that controls the reduction or reads ahead to it. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says only that the portraits are a mixed bag, and the acceptance line about edges holding on the green is the client's standing quality requirement. (c) It is not a propagation re-run, because the response is a different route per frame, an explicitly selected and inverted ground filled to the house colour rather than a one call knockout.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-plan the knockout route frame by frame, re-derive the affected plates through an explicit selection of the wall by its own material properties, inverted and filled, re-inspect each cut edge on the green rather than on white, and re-read both the reduction and the upscale entries in every tradeoffs object before any plate is bound.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Four producers appearing on their own neighbours' mail with a chewed collar and a halo against the house green, or eleven portraits brought to frame size by interpolation and printed soft at postcard scale.

deliverables.name: Aldervale autumn drop, press run and per producer subsets
deliverables.spec: One press file for the mail house with page count exactly equal to the drop list's row count, one household per page in the order the file was merged, every page carrying that household's own address complete to its final line, its own offer band and its assigned producer's own photograph. Plus eleven per producer files, each named for its producer, each containing only that producer's households, with identity guaranteed by how the subset was requested.

deliverables.name: Aldervale producer portrait set
deliverables.spec: Eleven producer portraits brought to one look across two shooting situations (one white point, one contrast, one head size in frame), knocked out onto the card's own ground with an edge that holds on the green rather than only against white, cropped to the template's real portrait proportion, named to the values the drop list binds by, and no output above its source frame's pixel dimensions. Delivered with a per frame parameter log and the file to producer reconciliation.

deliverables.name: Recovered Aldervale mark
deliverables.spec: The compound lockup recovered from a photograph of a printed business card as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque rectangle riding underneath, delivered as both a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, holding its shield ring and hairline rule at the size it actually reproduces on the card and remaining legible reversed out of the house green.

deliverables.name: Aldervale digital renewal set, card front, email header and square
deliverables.spec: One native editable document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, the card front at its true postcard trim in absolute units, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the recovered mark as real vector shapes, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source it was authored from, which is the durable half: the carrier edits the document next season and the source guarantees the design survives regardless.

deliverables.name: Printer note, mapping record and sign off board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the template's real frame inventory and the field mapping as finally verified, every household that could not be set completely and what was done about it, every reduction or enlargement any tool reported, the type used by role with family, foundry and numeric weight, what can and cannot honestly be promised about trim and bleed from artwork of this origin, and what to watch for when using the recovered mark. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the approved portrait set and the licensed frame with nothing silently dropped.

verifiers_auto.text: The press file's page count equals the drop list's row count exactly, and page N carries row N's household.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the delivered PDF and compare against the row count of the merged list, then spot read household names on the first, middle and last pages against the corresponding rows.

verifiers_auto.text: The prepared template contains every field the card carries, not a subset.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the IDML of the prepared template and grep the stories for each expected placeholder token, asserting the full set is present.

verifiers_auto.text: Each page's portrait differs across producers and matches the producer assigned to that page's household.
verifiers_auto.how: Extract the embedded images page by page, hash them, and check the distinct hash count equals the producer count and that each page's hash matches its row's producer.

verifiers_auto.text: Eleven per producer files exist, each named for a producer, and each file's page count equals that producer's row count in the list.
verifiers_auto.how: Read filenames and page counts and reconcile against a per producer tally of the list.

verifiers_auto.text: No delivered raster exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare every delivered file's dimensions against its source per the manifest and diff the captured tradeoffs objects against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG carries a viewBox and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.

verifiers_auto.how: Read the slide count and per slide dimensions from the export response, then parse the returned per slide markup for placeholder image data and count path shape elements in the mark's region.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_auto.text: The sign-off board exists as a persistent shareable board and carries every approved item with nothing silently dropped: the eleven approved producer plates plus the one licensed frame, twelve placements in all, with no failed placement.
verifiers_auto.how: Resolve the returned board id to a persistent shareable board, read its placed-item list and assert it holds exactly twelve items (the eleven producer plates plus the one licensed Stock frame), and assert the create/add responses report an empty failedItems array and no 201 partial status (the per-call cap is twelve, so a 201 partial would mean at least one item was dropped).

verifiers_auto.text: The one licensed Stock frame is a real photograph, IP-clean and not generative, and is placed at or below its licensed native resolution rather than enlarged.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the licensed Stock asset's metadata and assert isGenTech is false (not a generative candidate) and its contentType is photo (photography, not illustration or vector), then compare the delivered frame's pixel dimensions against the licensed download's native pixel dimensions and assert the delivered dimensions do not exceed the native ones (no upscale).

verifiers_human.text: Every card's address block ends where an address ends, postal line present, at trim.
verifiers_human.how: Read the address block on every page of the press file at trim size, with attention to the longest rows.

verifiers_human.how: View each card's portrait at full size against the green band, looking for a bitten collar, a halo or a soft shoulder.

verifiers_human.how: View the mark at its reproduction size on the card and on the green ground, not at full canvas.

verifiers_human.text: The card reads as a letter from a mutual the household already knows, not as a renewal blast and not as a private wealth invitation.
verifiers_human.how: Judge type register, offer prominence, photograph weight and margin against the stated band and the forty to seventy owner.

verifiers_human.how: Read the note against the run and confirm every reconciliation, every flagged household and every limitation is named.

decision_gates: Whether the template the client's own artwork produces can carry the fields the card shows, which the printed card cannot tell you and the readout will not tell you honestly.
Whether to author the mapping against the readout's convenient string or against the document's own reconstructed text.
Which of the three ambiguously named portrait files belongs to which producer, settled from faces and towns rather than filenames.
Knockout route per portrait: the one call route where shoulder contrast supports it, an explicitly selected and inverted ground filled to the house colour where it does not.
The portrait crop proportion, which is set by the converted template's real frame bounds rather than by what the printed card appears to show.
How the master file is ordered for the mail house, given that a producer's contiguous block and the mail house's order are two different sorts and only one can live in one file.
Per household copy fitting on the longest addresses: what can be legitimately shortened in a postal address and what has to be flagged back to the carrier instead.

Selection wording on the business card: naming the card takes the stock, naming the ink's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed shield is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the card, judged at reproduction size on the green rather than at full canvas.
Type substitution where a family named on a seven year old style guide page is no longer licensable, judged against the mutual's register rather than by resemblance.
How quietly the offer sits. At this band restraint is the design, and a bright benefit forward card is a correct looking wrong answer that costs retention.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of an insurance postcard. IDENTITY: these are eleven real producers whose actual faces have to appear on the mail going to their own towns, and the mark has to be RECOVERED off a photographed business card rather than reinvented, because a regenerated mark is a different carrier's mark on a regulated communication. SPEC: sixty households each need their own address, their own producer and their own compliance approved offer line, delivered as one press file whose page count equals the row count and as eleven correctly partitioned per producer files, none of which a generated image satisfies or can be checked for. EDITABILITY: the digital set exists because the offer dates move every year and the carrier explicitly intends to change it itself. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this template actually hold all of its fields, does this address end where an address ends, does this cut edge hold on the green.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, including building a live merge template from a bare PDF; one record per page with page count equal to row count is the confirmed PDF behaviour, recordRange subsetting is honoured, and per row image binding through an @ prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is visually confirmed to bind a different image per record. The checkpoints rest on documented live findings: textContent is LOSSY (a dropped 17 character run left every later offset short by 17, the validator returned VALID, prepare reported success, and 2 of 5 mappings silently failed to land); frame granularity from a PDF is not controllable; remove_background SILENTLY DOWNSCALES oversized inputs, reporting it only as a downscaled tradeoff entry, and crop_and_resize interpolates to a hard 2x cap reported only in its own tradeoffs. IMAGING: straighten, masked and unmasked adjustments, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert, crop_to_bounds, fill_area, remove_background in both forms and vectorize are verified across 27 live calls, with the substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the compound mark partial selection, the solid disc failure on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero all live findings. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export, absolute mm units, inline SVG as native editable vector and a genuine editable document findable by asset_search are all verified, and the rendition preview is first artboard only. FONTS, STOCK and BOARDS: find, styles, recommend and kit verified end to end; short Stock queries only with orientation never passed; boards capped at 12 placements per call with 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or merge, no variable QR, no bleed claim from a PDF sourced template, no pdfPreset, no naming of per record raster outputs by position, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photograph reaching Express as a URL, no batch above 20 files.
